name: Archaeological Site of Philippi
description: Philippi is a ruined walled city in north-eastern Greece, founded in 356 BC by Philip II of Macedon, Alexander the Great's father. It grew along the Via Egnatia, the road between Europe and Asia. Visitors can walk among the Hellenistic theatre and city walls, the Roman Forum and the remains of early Christian basilicas, built after the Apostle Paul's visit around 49–50 CE.
